news.title: Football: Jackson and England beaten in WAFF World Cup Last-16
news.lede: Manx amputee footballer, Sean Jackson and the England national amputee football side have suffered defeat in the Last-16 at this year's WAFF World Cup in Mexico. The international squad fell to a 2-1 defeat to Egypt yesterday (18 November), during which England took the lead through Sofyan Filali's first world cup goal. However, Egypt struck back with an equaliser before half-time before adding a second late on to progress to the quarter-final phase. For England, it's not the end of the tournament as they now enter the play-offs for positions 9th to 16th.

news.title: Why Lucas Digne should retire from international football and focus on PSG?
news.lede: Lucas Digne is an interesting topic of discussion during this international break . He wasn't called up to Zidane's recent France squad for the Nations League games against Italy (away) and Türkiye (home), despite being a mainstay under Deschamps.One could argue that missing out on the previous two France squads is a blessing in disguise, as it will motivate him to work harder. One could also argue that it would be harsh if the lasting memory people have of his international career is the penalty that he gave away against Spain in the World Cup semi-final, as he didn't see where Lamine Yamal was. In spite of this, there are several reasons why he should consider retiring from international football.

news.title: Amputee Football World Cup: Morocco target final and title, says Coach
news.lede: Morocco’s national amputee football team is targeting a place in the final and the title at the World Cup in Mexico, national team coach Othmane El Najmi said on Wednesday. Speaking to MAP following Morocco’s emphatic 4-1 victory over Italy in the Round of 16 in San Juan de los Lagos, the coach praised his players’ flawless run since the start of the tournament, recalling that the objective set from the outset was to go as far as possible in the competition. As for Thursday’s quarter-final against Angola, El Najmi warned that the match would be “intense and very closely contested”. He described the opponents as a “formidable” side, highlighting their impressive record: world champions in 2018, runners-up in 2022 in Turkey and fifth-place finishers at the last Africa Cup of Nations (CAN).
